videos.title: GMAT exam structure and official preparation
videos.by: GMAC, the organisation that runs the exam
videos.note: The authoritative source for format, scoring, fees and practice exams. Check it before you book.

books.title: GMAT Official Guide (current edition)
books.author: GMAC
books.sections: The review chapters for Quantitative Reasoning, Verbal Reasoning and Data Insights, then the practice questions in order of difficulty.
books.why: Real retired exam questions. Use these for all timed practice.

months.title: The language of business
months.subject: Financial and managerial accounting
months.summary: Read the three financial statements, judge a company by its ratios, understand costs and build a first business case.
months.gmat: Exam format, percentages and ratios, algebra, rates, critical reasoning, reading comprehension, data sufficiency, tables.

videos.title: Introduction to Financial Accounting
videos.note: The best-known MBA-level accounting course online. Weeks 1 to 4 match this month's Weeks 1 to 3.

videos.title: Accounting and financial statements
videos.note: Short, slow-paced videos. Use these first if the Wharton course feels fast.

books.title: Financial Intelligence
books.author: Karen Berman and Joe Knight
books.sections: Part Two (income statement), Part Three (balance sheet), Part Four (cash), Part Five (ratios), Part Six (ROI), Part Seven (working capital).
books.why: Written for managers who are not accountants. If you buy one book this month, buy this.

books.title: Romancing the Balance Sheet
books.author: Anil Lamba
books.sections: The chapters on reading the balance sheet, on funds flow and on working capital.
books.why: Indian examples and terminology, in plain language.

books.title: Cost Accounting: A Managerial Emphasis
books.author: Horngren, Datar and Rajan
books.sections: The chapters on cost-volume-profit analysis, activity-based costing, the master budget, and flexible budgets and variances.
books.why: The standard MBA text for Week 4. Chapter numbers differ between editions, so go by chapter title.

months.title: Markets and evidence
months.subject: Managerial economics and statistics
months.summary: How prices form, how competitors react, and how to reason from data without fooling yourself.
months.gmat: Number properties, exponents, inequalities, counting, assumption and evaluate questions, first official practice test.

videos.title: 14.01 Principles of Microeconomics
videos.note: A full university course. The lectures on supply and demand, elasticity, costs, monopoly and oligopoly cover Weeks 5 and 6.

videos.title: Game Theory (ECON 159)
videos.note: Lectures 1 to 6 are enough for Week 6. Very clear and entertaining.

videos.title: Statistics and probability
videos.note: Work through the units on summarising data, probability, sampling distributions, confidence intervals and significance tests for Weeks 7 and 8.

books.title: Principles of Economics
books.author: N. Gregory Mankiw
books.sections: The chapters on supply and demand, elasticity, the costs of production, competitive markets, monopoly and oligopoly.
books.why: The clearest introductory text. Any recent edition will do.

books.title: The Art of Strategy
books.author: Avinash Dixit and Barry Nalebuff
books.sections: Part I, especially the chapters on the prisoners' dilemma and on strategic moves.
books.why: Game theory through stories, with almost no mathematics.

books.title: Naked Statistics
books.author: Charles Wheelan
books.sections: The chapters on descriptive statistics, probability, the central limit theorem, inference, regression and programme evaluation.
books.why: Builds intuition before formulas. Read it alongside Weeks 7 and 8.

months.title: Money over time
months.subject: Corporate finance
months.summary: Value an investment properly: discounting, net present value, cost of capital and how companies are valued.
months.gmat: Two-part analysis, graphics, sets and statistics, harder critical reasoning, timed mixed sets.

videos.title: 15.401 Finance Theory I
videos.note: Full video lectures from the MIT Sloan MBA. The sessions on present value, capital budgeting, risk and return, and CAPM match Weeks 9 to 11.

videos.title: Introduction to Corporate Finance
videos.note: Shorter and more applied than the MIT course. Good for time value of money and NPV.

videos.title: Corporate finance and valuation classes
videos.note: His site links to free recordings of his full MBA classes, plus data on betas, risk premiums and multiples by industry and country. I could not load the page while writing this, so confirm the link works.

books.title: Principles of Corporate Finance
books.author: Brealey, Myers and Allen
books.sections: Chapter 2 (present values), chapters 5 and 6 (NPV and investment decisions), chapters 7 to 9 (risk and cost of capital), chapter 10 (project analysis), chapters 17 and 18 (debt policy).
books.why: The standard MBA finance text. Chapter numbers are from recent editions and may shift slightly.

books.title: The Little Book of Valuation
books.author: Aswath Damodaran
books.sections: The chapters on intrinsic valuation and on relative valuation.
books.why: Valuation in 200 small pages, by the person most associated with the subject.

books.title: Valuation: Measuring and Managing the Value of Companies
books.author: Koller, Goedhart and Wessels (McKinsey)
books.sections: Part One, on the foundations of value.
books.why: What consultants and bankers actually use. Read Part One only for now.

months.title: Customers and revenue
months.subject: Marketing, pricing and sales strategy
months.summary: Choose customers, position an offer, price on value and understand the economics of a subscription business.
months.gmat: Reading comprehension at speed, inference questions, table analysis, harder data sufficiency, timed sets.

videos.title: Introduction to Marketing
videos.by: Barbara Kahn, Peter Fader and Jagmohan Raju, Wharton, on Coursera
videos.note: Covers positioning, customer centricity and go-to-market. Fader's part on customer value fits Week 16 well.

books.title: Obviously Awesome
books.author: April Dunford
books.sections: Part 2, the components of positioning, and Part 3, the ten-step process.
books.why: The most practical book on positioning for B2B technology.

books.title: Crossing the Chasm
books.author: Geoffrey Moore
books.sections: Part 1 on the adoption life cycle, then the chapters on targeting the point of attack and on the whole product.
books.why: The standard account of how technology products reach mainstream industrial buyers.

books.title: The Strategy and Tactics of Pricing
books.author: Thomas Nagle and Georg Müller
books.sections: The chapters on value creation, price structure and value communication.
books.why: The reference on value-based pricing.

books.title: Monetizing Innovation
books.author: Madhavan Ramanujam and Georg Tacke
books.sections: Chapters 1 to 4, then the chapters on segmentation and price structure.
books.why: How to design the price before the product. Useful for anyone heading towards product management.

books.title: Marketing Management
books.author: Philip Kotler and Kevin Lane Keller
books.sections: The chapters on market segments and targets, business markets, and marketing channels.
books.why: The comprehensive MBA text. Use it as a reference.

months.title: Making and moving things
months.subject: Operations and supply chain management
months.summary: Your home ground, at MBA depth: process analysis, variability, quality and supply chain strategy as a general manager sees them.
months.gmat: Timed review sets in all three sections and a second official practice test.

videos.title: Introduction to Operations Management
videos.note: Process analysis, productivity, variability and quality, taught by the co-author of the main textbook. Follows Weeks 17 to 19 closely.

videos.title: MicroMasters in Supply Chain Management
videos.note: Far more than you need. The first course, on supply chain analytics, deepens Weeks 18 and 20 if you want it.

books.title: The Goal
books.author: Eliyahu Goldratt
books.sections: All of it. It is a novel and reads in a weekend.
books.why: On most MBA operations reading lists. The bottleneck idea stays with you for life.

books.title: Matching Supply with Demand
books.author: Gérard Cachon and Christian Terwiesch
books.sections: The chapters on process capacity, variability and waiting time, the newsvendor model, and risk pooling.
books.why: The MBA operations text, quantitative and clear.

books.title: Factory Physics
books.author: Wallace Hopp and Mark Spearman
books.sections: The chapters on variability basics and on the corrupting influence of variability.
books.why: The deepest treatment of why factories behave as they do. An engineer will enjoy it.

books.title: The Toyota Way
books.author: Jeffrey Liker
books.sections: Part Two, the fourteen principles.
books.why: Lean as a management system, not a toolkit.

months.title: Where to compete and how to win
months.subject: Strategy and macroeconomics
months.summary: Analyse an industry, explain why some firms stay profitable, and read the economy that surrounds them.
months.gmat: Harder drills in every section, based on your practice test results.

videos.title: Foundations of Business Strategy
videos.by: Michael Lenox and Jared Harris, Darden (University of Virginia), on Coursera
videos.note: Industry analysis, competitive advantage and strategy formulation with short cases. Matches Weeks 21 and 22.

videos.title: Macroeconomics
videos.note: Units on GDP, inflation, monetary and fiscal policy and exchange rates for Week 24.

books.title: Good Strategy Bad Strategy
books.author: Richard Rumelt
books.sections: Chapters 1 to 5, ending with the kernel of good strategy.
books.why: The clearest statement of what strategy is and is not.

books.title: Understanding Michael Porter
books.author: Joan Magretta
books.sections: Chapters 1 to 4.
books.why: Porter's ideas in 200 readable pages, checked by Porter himself.

books.title: 7 Powers
books.author: Hamilton Helmer
books.sections: The seven chapters, one for each power.
books.why: The best framework for judging whether an advantage will last.

books.title: The Innovator's Dilemma
books.author: Clayton Christensen
books.sections: Chapters 1, 2 and 5.
books.why: The original account of disruption.

books.title: Playing to Win
books.author: A.G. Lafley and Roger Martin
books.sections: Chapter 1, the five choices.
books.why: A practical structure for writing a strategy.

months.title: Leading people
months.subject: Organisational behaviour, leadership and negotiation
months.summary: Motivate a team, design an organisation, lead change and negotiate. This is the material most engineers skip and most senior roles depend on.
months.gmat: Timed sectional drills, an error-log clinic and a third practice test.

videos.title: Introduction to Negotiation
videos.note: Rigorous and practical, with negotiation exercises. The first three modules cover Week 27.

videos.title: Managing Social and Human Capital
videos.by: Michael Useem and Peter Cappelli, Wharton, on Coursera
videos.note: Motivation, reward systems, organisation design and leading change. Matches Weeks 25 and 26.

books.title: High Output Management
books.author: Andrew Grove
books.sections: The chapters on managerial leverage, meetings and one-on-ones, task-relevant maturity and performance appraisal.
books.why: Written by an engineer who ran Intel. The best single book for a first-time manager.

books.title: Getting to Yes
books.author: Roger Fisher, William Ury and Bruce Patton
books.sections: Chapters 1 to 6.
books.why: The foundation of modern negotiation teaching.

books.title: Leading Change
books.author: John Kotter
books.sections: Chapters 1 and 2, then the eight steps.
books.why: The standard model for the work you say you want to lead.

books.title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
books.author: Daniel Kahneman
books.sections: Part II (heuristics and biases) and Part III (overconfidence).
books.why: The research behind every decision-making session in this course.

books.title: The Pyramid Principle
books.author: Barbara Minto
books.sections: Part One, logic in writing.
books.why: How consultants structure everything they write.

months.title: Putting it together
months.subject: Product, digital strategy and capstone
months.summary: Product management, technology strategy and entrepreneurship, ending with a full board-level recommendation and exam readiness.
months.gmat: Final reviews, two full mock exams under test conditions and a test-day plan.

videos.title: Digital Product Management: Modern Fundamentals
videos.by: Alex Cowan, Darden (University of Virginia), on Coursera
videos.note: Discovery, hypothesis-driven development and working with engineering. Matches Week 29.

videos.title: AI For Everyone
videos.note: A non-technical course on what AI can and cannot do and how to choose projects. Matches Week 30.

videos.title: Startup School
videos.note: Free course for founders. The sessions on evaluating ideas, talking to users and unit economics fit Week 31.

books.title: Inspired
books.author: Marty Cagan
books.sections: The parts on the right people and on product discovery.
books.why: The reference book on modern product management.

books.title: Prediction Machines
books.author: Ajay Agrawal, Joshua Gans and Avi Goldfarb
books.sections: Parts One and Two.
books.why: An economist's way to judge any AI use case. It will outlast any particular technology.

books.title: Competing in the Age of AI
books.author: Marco Iansiti and Karim Lakhani
books.sections: Chapters 1 to 5.
books.why: How software and data change the way firms scale.

books.title: The Lean Startup
books.author: Eric Ries
books.sections: Part One and the chapter on testing.
books.why: Build, measure, learn, at the source.

books.title: The Mom Test
books.author: Rob Fitzpatrick
books.sections: All of it. About 130 pages.
books.why: How to talk to customers so that they tell you the truth.
